editorial_reason: The adjacency-matrix definition explicitly assumes a finite simple undirected graph. The independently screened unordered-doubleton simple-graph definition supplies that underlying structure; vertex finiteness and ordering remain further conditions.

A bipartite graph cannot contain loops, because every edge must cross two disjoint vertex classes. The new loopless undirected multigraph meaning permits parallel edges and is therefore broad enough for the bipartite definition without incorrectly demanding a simple graph.

The simple-graph edge set is explicitly a subset of all unordered two-element subsets of V. The set-theoretic subset relation is a genuine prerequisite for this construction, not an assumption of graph finiteness.

Each underlying edge type in a loopless undirected multigraph is a two-element subset of its vertex set. This foundational subset relation is needed even though E is a multiset and can contain parallel copies.
